Aristóteles fundó la lógica en el siglo: Aristotle founded logic in the fourth century BC and for more than two thousand years nobody improved on it in any substantial way; Kant went so far as to write that it was finished and closed. He was wrong. In 1847 George Boole published a book with a telling title, The Mathematical Analysis of Logic, in which he turned reasoning into algebra: true was 1, false was 0, and the connectives were operations. Nobody saw any practical use for it. Ninety years later a student named Claude Shannon realised that those zeros and ones described switching circuits exactly, and wrote with that idea the most influential master's thesis in history.

Confusing an implication with its converse is the error that costs most dearly outside the classroom. A medical test satisfies “if you are ill, it comes out positive”; that does not mean “if it comes out positive, you are ill”. With a rare disease, most positives can be false even if the test is excellent. What is always valid is the contrapositive: “if it comes out negative, you are not ill”. You will come back to this, with numbers, in conditional probability.
